newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai shares end sharply down on crackdown fear.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai shares end sharply down on crackdown fear.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended down 9.267 points or 12.26 percent at 66.291 points on Friday on fears that Beijing would crack down on domestic investors trading B shares, traders said.

The fears were sparked by news reports that the securities authorities in Shenzhen had ordered local brokerages not to accept foreign exchange to buy B shares from local people unless they proved the money originated from outside China, they said.
Shanghai's A share index lost 67.781 points or 5.51 percent to 1,163.050 on news that checks had begun in some parts of China on the risk management systems of securities brokerages.
Volume was 56.4 million shares worth $23.3 million. All 42 B shares traded and fell.
Brokers said that the sharp fall on the Shenzhen B share market caused by the local crackdown on domestic investors buying fueled market fears and both profit-taking and liquidation selling emerged.

"Everyone fears the securities authorities will announce new measures to prevent domestic investors from buying as the market has been too speculative in the past few days with a little easing of the rules," one broker said.

"The index will find support around 62 points and the market will rally again next week if there is no fresh market news," a second broker said. "Falls in the past three days has made the market over-sold."
Shanghai Automation Instrumentation was the biggest loser, slipping $0.062 or 21.37 percent to $0.228, on volume of 1.7 million shares.
Shanghai Sewing Machine followed, closing down $0.052 or 19.84 percent to $0.210, on volume of 702,000 shares.
Shanghai Worldbest traded the most on institutional liquidation, falling $0.074 or 17.05 percent to $0.360, on volume of 3.5 million shares.
Shanghai A shares tumbled largely on announcements that local governments in several parts of China had begun checks on the risk management measures of securities institutions, brokers said.

The A index closed down 67.781 points or 5.51 percent to 1163.050 points, on volume of 863.5 million shares worth 9.6 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index slipped 172.219 points or 5.83 percent to 2780.534 points.
Jifa Development was the biggest loser, falling 3.30 yuan or 17.83 percent to 15.20 yuan on volume of 5.5 million shares.
